title: Stroke-Dysphagia Care-Transition FHIR Implementation Guide
description:
An open, standards-aligned HL7 FHIR R4 Implementation Guide that makes stroke-dysphagia care-transition data computable across the acute, inpatient-rehabilitation, and home/tele-rehabilitation journey, together with a structured terminology-gap analysis (SNOMED CT, LOINC) and an executable decision-support feasibility evaluation in Clinical Quality Language run on a real engine over a synthetic Synthea cohort.

The repository contains six FHIR R4 profiles, six ValueSets (including the two IDDSI axes), a local CodeSystem for instruments that currently lack terminology, an AspirationRiskAlert CQL rule, a conformance harness (eight positive examples on two deployments that share the HL7 validation core, so this shows portability rather than independence across implementations; eight negative fixtures on both deployments), and a fully containerized, seeded evaluation pipeline. Releases 1.1.2 and 1.1.3 added the deposited 333-bundle evaluation cohort, the generator run record, the reference validator QA output and two further supplementary files. Release 1.2.0 moves the aspiration-risk flag pattern onto the CodeableConcept, so an instance carrying a site local code alongside the SNOMED translation now conforms, and adds a harness that validates every deposited cohort bundle against the built IG. Release 1.2.1 carries the third-party licence notice in the copyright element of every conformance resource (an IG-level notice does not propagate to them) with a repository NOTICE for the instance resources FHIR gives no such element, corrects one negative fixture that carried a non-verbatim display term, runs the negative suite on both deployments, stamps each conformance record with the IG version and run time, and lets the parameter sweep read the deposited cohort so every reported result is reproducible from the archive alone. Release 1.2.2 extends the negative suite to ten fixtures so that every constraint Table 1 names is exercised (including Composition.type and section.entry), deposits a reference-validator record for the positive suite as well so that both deployments denotes the same pair for both suites, and carries the Global Patient Set attribution and licence URI in the copyright element of the value sets that actually carry SNOMED display terms.

Scope and claims. All data are synthetic or drawn from the published literature. No human or animal subjects, no patient data, and no clinical-benefit or diagnostic claim are involved; the evaluation demonstrates interoperability and computability feasibility, not clinical validity.

Terminology notice. This IG references SNOMED CT, LOINC, and IDDSI codes; it does not redistribute their code systems. The MIT license covers only the source and IG artifacts authored here.
